title: Cities Within Radius: What Falls in the Circle
description: List the cities that fall within a radius of a centre point with Cities Within Radius — straight-line, ranked, honest about the edges. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 50-mile circle around Chicago takes in Oak Park (8.0 mi), Evanston (11.7), Gary (24.5), Naperville (28.4) and Joliet (33.7) — while Milwaukee, at 81.4 miles, waits outside.
quick_answer: Cities Within Radius lists the cities and towns whose centres fall inside a circle you draw around a point. Set the centre and radius and read the ranked list — every place inside, sorted by distance, for market scans, relocation shortlists and every 'what is near here, really?' question.

Which towns does a depot's 50-mile promise really cover? The list is the promise, itemised — catchments drawn by straight line, before drive-time refinements.
A central venue's realistic catchment is the towns in its circle. Invitation lists built from the circle stop forgetting the near town in the next county.
Listings love the phrase 'near Chicago'. The circle adjudicates: Gary at 24.5 miles is near; Milwaukee at 81.4 is a different claim entirely.

In: Oak Park 8.0 mi, Evanston 11.7, Gary 24.5, Naperville 28.4, Joliet 33.7. Out: Milwaukee 81.4. The list is sorted by centre-to-centre distance — Gary's presence reminds you the circle crosses state lines without asking permission.

examples.label: Example · Centre of the city, edge of the town

body.t: Membership is judged at each city's centre point. A big city's edge can be inside your circle while its centre is outside — the list says which convention it used, and the radius you choose should leave slack for it.

faq: Which cities are in the underlying list?

A gazetteer of incorporated places and recognised towns with their centre coordinates — deep in the US and Europe, thinner where settlement data is sparse. The list states its source family so gaps read as data limits, not editorial choices.
Why is a city I can see on the map missing?

Its centre may fall just outside the circle even while its suburbs reach in — or the gazetteer's threshold skipped a very small place. Both are conventions, stated here so you can widen the radius deliberately.
The default order is distance. Population context belongs to the Population Within Radius tool, which counts people instead of places.
Yes — radii enter in miles or kilometres, per this site's convention, and distances report in both.
The circle is blind to borders, lakes and tolls: Gary, Indiana is in Chicago's circle and across a state line. Political and physical reality layer on top of the geometry, by your judgment.
Each listed place counts separately even inside one metro — the list is of municipalities, not metro areas, and says so.
How big can the radius be?
Continental radii return continental lists — technically fine, editorially useless. The tool serves local and regional questions best.
Yes: great-circle distance between the two centre points, computed on the sphere. It is not a boundary-to-boundary measure; edge cases near the line deserve the slack the examples describe.
